steps.message:
## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

{"status": "ok", "filepath": "rich/_inspect.py", "content": "import inspect
from inspect import cleandoc, getdoc, getfile, isclass, ismodule, signature
from typing import Any, Collection, Iterable, Optional, Tuple, Type, Union

from .console import Group, RenderableType
from .control import escape_control_codes
from .highlighter import ReprHighlighter
from .jupyter import JupyterMixin
from .panel import Panel
from .pretty import Pretty
from .table import Table
from .text import Text, TextType


def _first_paragraph(doc: str) -> str:
    """Get the first paragraph from a docstring."""
    paragraph, _, _ = doc.partition("\n\n")
    return paragraph


class Inspect(JupyterMixin):
    """A renderable to inspect any Python Object.

    Args:
        obj (Any): An object to inspect.
        title (str, optional): Title to display over inspect result, or None use type. Defaults to None.
        help (bool, optional): Show full help text rather than just first paragraph. Defaults to False.
        methods (bool, optional): Enable inspection of callables. Defaults to False.
        docs (bool, optional): Also render doc strings. Defaults to True.
        private (bool, optional): Show private attributes (beginning with underscore). Defaults to False.
        dunder (bool, optional): Show attributes starting with double underscore. Defaults to False.
        sort (bool, optional): Sort attributes alphabetically. Defaults to True.
        all (bool, optional): Show all attributes. Defaults to False.
        value (bool, optional): Pretty print value of object. Defaults to True.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        obj: Any,
        *,
        title: Optional[TextType] = None,
        help: bool = False,
        methods: bool = False,
        docs: bool = True,
        private: bool = False,
        dunder: bool = False,
        sort: bool = True,
        all: bool = True,
        value: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        self.highlighter = ReprHighlighter()
        self.obj = obj
        self.title = title or self._make_title(obj)
        if all:
            methods = private = dunder = True
        self.help = help
        self.methods = methods
        self.docs = docs or help
        self.private = private or dunder
        self.dunder = dunder
        self.sort = sort
        self.value = value

    def _make_title(self, obj: Any) -> Text:
        """Make a default title."""
        title_str = (
            str(obj)
            if (isclass(obj) or callable(obj) or ismodule(obj))
            else str(type(obj))
        )
        title_text = self.highlighter(title_str)
        return title_text

    def __rich__(self) -> Panel:
        return Panel.fit(
            Group(*self._render()),
            title=self.title,
            border_style="scope.border",
            padding=(0, 1),
        )

    def _get_signature(self, name: str, obj: Any) -> Optional[Text]:
        """Get a signature for a callable."""
        try:
            _signature = str(signature(obj)) + ":"
        except ValueError:
            _signature = "(...)"
        except TypeError:
            return None

        source_filename: Optional[str] = None
        try:
            source_filename = getfile(obj)
        except (OSError, TypeError):
            # OSError is raised if obj has no source file, e.g. when defined in REPL.
            pass

        callable_name = Text(name, style="inspect.callable")
        if source_filename:
            callable_name.stylize(f"link file://{source_filename}")
        signature_text = self.highlighter(_signature)

        qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)

        # If obj is a module, there may be classes (which are callable) to display
        if inspect.isclass(obj):
            prefix = "class"
        elif inspect.iscoroutinefunction(obj):
            prefix = "async def"
        else:
            prefix = "def"

        qual_signature = Text.assemble(
            (f"{prefix} ", f"inspect.{prefix.replace(' ', '_')}"),
            (qualname, "inspect.callable"),
            signature_text,
        )

        return qual_signature

    def _render(self) -> Iterable[RenderableType]:
        """Render object."""

        def sort_items(item: Tuple[str, Any]) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
            key, (_error, value) = item
            return (callable(value), key.strip("_").lower())

        def safe_getattr(attr_name: str) -> Tuple[Any, Any]:
            """Get attribute or any exception."""
            try:
                return (None, getattr(obj, attr_name))
            except Exception as error:
                return (error, None)

        obj = self.obj
        keys = dir(obj)
        total_items = len(keys)
        if not self.dunder:
            keys = [key for key in keys if not key.startswith("__")]
        if not self.private:
            keys = [key for key in keys if not key.startswith("_")]
        not_shown_count = total_items - len(keys)
        items = [(key, safe_getattr(key)) for key in keys]
        if self.sort:
            items.sort(key=sort_items)

        items_table = Table.grid(padding=(0, 1), expand=False)
        items_table.add_column(justify="right")
        add_row = items_table.add_row
        highlighter = self.highlighter", "start_line": 1, "end_line": 150, "total_lines": 268, "is_truncated": false}
